correctness.rationale: For a quartic graph each edge has six neighbours. A red edge uv forces r(u)+r(v)=5, a blue edge forces r(u)+r(v)=3. The five red-degree types form the forced connected transition chain 0,3,2,1,4, exactly the distance layers of the zero-red set, with neighbour counts (i,4-i). Conversely alternate edge colours between consecutive layers give red degrees 0,3,2,1,4 and meet the exact per-edge condition. Double-counting consecutive cross-edges gives sizes (a,4a,6a,4a,a), hence order 16a, and opposite parity layers give bipartiteness. All 16 singleton centers were checked in the two order-16 graphs, and different four-cycle totals certify non-isomorphism. The standalone executable verifies independently by direct edge condition; no finite experiment is used to infer the unrestricted theorem.

evidence: Earlier 2026 papers imply structural degree parity at most, while new theorem implies connected bipartite graph order divisible by 16 plus a bijection with exactly specified code sets.

Freyberg–Marr imply a 6-regular line graph with an NBC has equal numbers of coloured vertices and divisible-by-four edge count. This falls short of a quartic-root order divisible by 16 or a five-layer code bijection.
Historical same-area cubic-graph bijection concerns 3-regular graphs and efficient radius-one dominating sets; its hypotheses exclude the present 4-regular graph.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Even-degree quartic graphs such as K5 do not satisfy the new iff, so broad upper bounds and necessary parity do not imply it. The code object has radius four rather than the radius-one efficient domination used in the unrelated cubic classification. Sources were compared by exact implications, not titles alone.

evidence: A strong-majority 2-edge-colouring of a quartic graph is exactly a neighbourhood-balanced 2-vertex-colouring of its 6-regular line graph, since every edge sees 6 adjacent edges.
Freyberg–Marr (2024), Section 1 NBC definition and Section 3 Theorem 9 classify 4-regular *circulants*, not 6-regular line graphs of arbitrary quartic graphs.
A code with the prescribed intersection array is a completely regular code; the present theorem characterizes when that object exists and counts the associated colourings.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The equivalent line-graph formulation is taken seriously: general NBC balance theorems restrict red/blue class sizes, whereas the specific line-graph root constraints force the five-layer quartic-root structure; neither cited article states the latter universal bijection.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 strong-majority edge-colouring problem lacked an exact two-colour quartic classification. A universal bijection with the strongly structured four-cube completely regular codes is mathematically informative: it yields nontrivial sharp order divisibility and bipartiteness, exact interpretation of the colouring count and two differently enumerated minimum-order graph examples. The passage from edge constraints to distance layers is an explanatory structural result for an unrestricted infinite class, not a mere restatement of an existing upper bound.
